{{Short description|Force on magnetic flux tubes}}
In [[plasma physics]], '''magnetic buoyancy''' is an upward force exerted on [[magnetic flux tube]]s that are immersed in [[electrically conducting]] fluids and are under the influence of a [[gravitational force]]. It acts on magnetic flux tubes in [[Convection zone|stellar convection zones]] where it plays an important role in the formation of [[sunspot]]s and [[starspot]]s.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Guerrero |first1=G. |last2=Käpylä |first2=P. J. |title=Dynamo action and magnetic buoyancy in convection simulations with vertical shear |journal=Astronomy & Astrophysics |date=September 2011 |volume=533 |pages=A40 |doi=10.1051/0004-6361/201116749 |arxiv=1102.3598 |bibcode=2011A&A...533A..40G |s2cid=118582079 }}</ref> It was first proposed by [[Eugene Parker]] in 1955.

==Magnetic flux tubes==
For a magnetic flux tube in [[hydrostatic equilibrium]] with the surrounding medium, the tube's interior [[magnetic pressure]] <math>p_m</math> and [[fluid pressure]] <math>p_i</math> must be balanced by the fluid pressure <math>p_e</math> of the exterior medium, that is,
:<math>p_e = p_i + p_m.</math>
The magnetic pressure is always positive, so <math>p_e > p_i.</math> As such, assuming that the temperature of the plasma within the flux tube is the same as the temperature of the surrounding plasma, the density of the flux tube must be lower than the density of the surrounding medium. Under the influence of a gravitational force, the tube will rise.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Parker |first1=Eugene N. |title=The Formation of Sunspots from the Solar Toroidal Field. |journal=The Astrophysical Journal |date=March 1955 |volume=121 |pages=491 |doi=10.1086/146010 |bibcode=1955ApJ...121..491P |url=https://articles.adsabs.harvard.edu/pdf/1955ApJ...121..491P}}</ref><ref name="acheson79" />

==Instability==
The '''magnetic buoyancy instability''' is a [[plasma instability]] that can arise from small perturbations in systems where magnetic buoyancy is present. The magnetic buoyancy instability in a system with magnetic field <math>\mathbf{B}</math> and perturbation [[wavevector]] <math>\mathbf{k}</math>, has three modes: the '''interchange instability''' where the perturbation wavevector is perpendicular to the magnetic field direction <math>\left(\mathbf{k}\perp\mathbf{B}\right)</math>; the '''undular instability''', sometimes referred to as the '''Parker instability''' or '''magnetic Rayleigh–Taylor instability''', where the perturbation wavevector is parallel to the magnetic field direction <math>\left(\mathbf{k}\parallel\mathbf{B}\right)</math>; and the '''mixed instability''', sometimes referred to as the '''quasi-interchange instability''', a combination of the interchange and undular instabilities.<ref name="acheson79">{{cite journal |last1=Acheson |first1=D. J. |authorlink1=David Acheson (mathematician) |title=Instability by magnetic buoyancy |journal=Solar Physics |date=May 1979 |volume=62 |issue=1 |pages=23–50 |doi=10.1007/BF00150129 |bibcode=1979SoPh...62...23A |s2cid=121629539 |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF00150129|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Matsumoto |first1=R. |last2=Tajima |first2=T. |last3=Shibata |first3=K. |last4=Kaisig |first4=M. |title=Three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamics of the emerging magnetic flux in the solar atmosphere |journal=The Astrophysical Journal |date=September 1993 |volume=414 |pages=357 |doi=10.1086/173082 |bibcode=1993ApJ...414..357M |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gilman |first1=Peter A. |title=Magnetic Buoyancy and Rotational Instabilities in the Tachocline |journal=The Astrophysical Journal |date=24 January 2018 |volume=853 |issue=1 |pages=65 |doi=10.3847/1538-4357/aaa4f4 |bibcode=2018ApJ...853...65G |s2cid=126268222 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kim |first1=J. |last2=Ryu |first2=D. |last3=Hong |first3=S. S. |last4=Lee |first4=S. M. |last5=Franco |first5=J. |title=The Parker Instability |journal=How Does the Galaxy Work? |series=Astrophysics and Space Science Library |date=2005 |volume=315 |pages=315–322 |doi=10.1007/1-4020-2620-X_65 |isbn=1-4020-2619-6 |url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/1-4020-2620-X_65|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Parker instability in astrophysics ==
In [[astrophysics]], the '''Parker instability''' is a [[Magnetohydrodynamics|magnetohydrodynamic]] [[instability]] in a gas layer where a horizontal [[magnetic field]] supports gas against [[gravity]], causing it to become buoyant and rise.<ref name=dict/> This buoyancy, driven by magnetic fields and [[cosmic ray]] pressure, leads to the formation of magnetic loops, gas outflow, and can influence [[star formation]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Tharakkal |first1=Devika |last2=Shukurov |first2=Anvar |last3=Gent |first3=Frederick A. |last4=Sarson |first4=Graeme R. |last5=Snodin |first5=Andrew |title=Steady states of the Parker instability: The effects of rotation |journal=Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society |date=2023 |volume=525 |issue=2 |pages=2972–2984 |doi=10.1093/mnras/stad2475 |doi-access=free }}</ref> and the structure of the [[interstellar medium]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Heintz |first1=Evan |last2=Bustard |first2=Chad |last3=Zweibel |first3=Ellen G. |title=The Role of the Parker Instability in Structuring the Interstellar Medium |journal=The Astrophysical Journal |date=2020 |volume=891 |issue=2 |page=157 |doi=10.3847/1538-4357/ab7453 |arxiv=1910.03588 |bibcode=2020ApJ...891..157H |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lee |first1=Sang Min |last2=Hong |first2=S. S. |title=Parker Instability in a Self-Gravitating Magnetized Gas Disk. III. Nonlinear Development of the Parker Instability |journal=The Astrophysical Journal |date=2011 |volume=734 |issue=2 |page=101 |doi=10.1088/0004-637X/734/2/101 |bibcode=2011ApJ...734..101L }}</ref> It is a fundamental process affecting galactic dynamics and is modified by factors like rotation, cooling, and the degree of cosmic ray isotropy. It is sometimes called '''magnetic buoyancy'''.<ref name=dict>{{cite web | title=An Etymological Dictionary of Astronomy and Astrophysics - English-French-Persian |url=https://dictionary.obspm.fr/index.php?showAll=1&formSearchTextfield=Parker+instability}}</ref> Parker instability is a [[Rayleigh–Taylor instability|Rayleigh-Taylor-like instability]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Rodrigues |first1=L. F. S. |last2=Sarson |first2=G. R. |last3=Shukurov |first3=A. |last4=Bushby |first4=P. J. |last5=Fletcher |first5=A. |title=The Parker Instability in Disk Galaxies |journal=The Astrophysical Journal |date=2016 |volume=816 |issue=1 |page=2 |doi=10.3847/0004-637X/816/1/2 |arxiv=1510.06318 |bibcode=2016ApJ...816....2R |doi-access=free }}</ref>

It was first studied by [[Eugene Parker]] in 1966.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Parker |first1=E. N. |title=The Dynamical State of the Interstellar Gas and Field |journal=The Astrophysical Journal |date=1966 |volume=145 |page=811 |doi=10.1086/148828 |bibcode=1966ApJ...145..811P |url=https://adsabs.harvard.edu/full/1966ApJ...145..811P}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |title=The dynamical state of the interstellar gas and field. II. Non-linear growth of clouds and forces in three dimensions
|first=E.N. |last=Parker
|journal=Astrophysical Journal |volume= 149 |year=1967 |page=517 |doi=10.1086/149282 |url=https://adsabs.harvard.edu/full/record/seri/ApJ../0149/1967ApJ...149..517P.html}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |title=The Dynamical State of the Interstellar Gas and Field. III. Turbulence and Enhanced Diffusion |first=E.N. |last=Parker
|journal=Astrophysical Journal |volume=149 |year=1967 |page=535 |doi=10.1086/149283 |url=https://adsabs.harvard.edu/full/record/seri/ApJ../0149/1967ApJ...149..535P.html}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |title=The Dynamical State of the Interstellar Gas and Field. VI. Instability and Enhanced Diffusion in a Twisted Field |first1=I. |last1=Lerche |first2=E.N. |last2=Parker |journal=Astrophysical Journal |volume=154 |year=1968 |page=515 |doi=10.1086/149778 |bibcode=1968ApJ...154..515L |url=https://adsabs.harvard.edu/full/1968ApJ...154..515L}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Parker |first1=E.N. |title=Galactic effects of the cosmic-ray gas |journal=Space Science Reviews |date=1969 |volume=9 |issue=5 |page=651 |doi=10.1007/BF00174032 |bibcode=1969SSRv....9..651P |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF00174032|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Parker instability is associated with [[molecular cloud]] formation, and can be triggered in the arms of spiral galaxies.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Basu |first1=Shantanu |last2=Mouschovias |first2=Telemachos Ch. |last3=Paleologou |first3=Efthimios V. |title=Dynamical Effects of the Parker Instability in the Interstellar Medium |journal=The Astrophysical Journal |date=1997 |volume=480 |issue=1 |pages=L55–L58 |doi=10.1086/310620 |bibcode=1997ApJ...480L..55B |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1086/310620/fulltext/}}</ref>
